title: Nested Squares and Distinct-Prime Goldbach Partitions
content: The distinct-prime Goldbach conjecture asserts that for every \( N\geq 4 \) there is \( M\in A_N=[1,N-3] \) with \( N-M \) and \( N+M \) both prime; geometrically, nested squares of side lengths \( N \) and \( M \) have an L-shaped difference of semiprime area \( (N-M)(N+M) \). With \( C_N \) and \( D_N \) the sets of \( M\in A_N \) for which \( N-M \), respectively $N+M$, is prime, the conjecture for \( 2N \) is \( C_N\cap D_N\neq\varnothing \). We embed this centered condition in a straddling one: \( C_N\cap D_N \) lies in the set \( E_N \) of half-differences \( (Q-P)/2\in A_N \) of primes $2<P<N<Q<2N$. From Mikawa's theorem on prime pairs with almost all differences we deduce \( |A_N\setminus E_N|\ll_D N/(\log N)^D \) for every \( D>0 \), and with explicit constants we prove \( |E_N|>N/760 \) for every \( N\geq 3275 \). Consequently, for all large \( N \) and all but \( O_D(N/(\log N)^D) \) primes $P<N$, the number \( 2N-P \) becomes prime after adding the difference \( P'-P \) of two primes $P'<N$; Goldbach's partition is the case \( P'=P \). In contrast, \( |C_N\cap D_N|<(N-3)-\log^2(2N) \) for every \( N\geq 34 \), and covering all but \( \log^2(2N) \) values of \( A_N \) for all large \( N \) would imply the Cram\'er-type bound \( p'-p<2\log^2(2p+2)+2 \). The method also shows that \( 2N \) is a sum of two distinct primes for more than \( X/9600 \) integers \( N\leq X \), for every \( X\geq 10^6 \). Computations up to \( N=10^6 \) compare the number of distinct-prime partitions with the Hardy--Littlewood prediction and measure the missing values of \( E_N \) forced by prime gaps. The conjecture itself is not proved here. dummy
